title: ChainProv-City: Governance-Aware Blockchain Provenance for Accountable Multi-Agency Verification of Smart City Events
content: Smart cities are moving to depend on big data and AI-focused data streams for key decisions, yet existing frameworks are often based on centralised architectures that are manipulable, with poor auditability, and deepfakes present a huge risk. ChainProv-City is an authority-based blockchain provenance system that provides trust and accountability in a smart city surveillance context. Unlike traditional approaches based on anonymous consensus, the model introduces institutional authorities into the validation process, ensuring that validation aligns with real-world governance frameworks. Each event is anchored in a device-signature commitment, adjudicated by k-of-m identity-bound agency votes with timeouts and a safety escalation route, and recorded in a hash-linked provenance trail; membership changes are managed by a separate governance quorum. Security is analysed in an explicit adversary model, and a representative deepfake case is simulated as executable tests. The Solidity prototype passes 24 automated tests. Registration consumes about 265k gas, a vote about 82k gas, throughput is limited by the block gas limit to about 56 events/s (66 with batching) and the median decision latency is below 4.0 s (excluding human review time). ChainProv-City is governance-aware event management which is an intermediate between blockchain provenance and smart cities.
